summary: An excerpt from Book 11 (part 111) of a novel, set at Wareham, in which Adam Ladd and Miss Maxwell discuss the overworked young Rebecca. Adam, who has been planning a prize-essay competition to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the Wareham schools, leaves a visit with the principal Mr. Morrison and then calls on Miss Maxwell. The two agree that Rebecca needs rest, and Miss Maxwell proposes taking her on her usual spring trip South, with Adam offering to help pay for it.
one_line: Adam Ladd and Miss Maxwell agree to take overworked Rebecca on a spring vacation South, while Adam plans essay prizes for Wareham schools.
key_facts: Adam Ladd tells Rebecca she is studying too hard and calls her Miss Rebecca Rowena.
Rebecca confesses she is studying 'Just a little' and notes that vacation comes soon.
Rebecca's eyes suffuse when Adam asks whether she will recover her dimples, and she says 'it's not one of my dimply days!'
This year is the fiftieth anniversary of the founding of the Wareham schools.
Adam plans to give a hundred volumes to the reference library and offer prizes in English composition.
The prizes are for the writers of the two best essays from the two upper classes, in money or books.
Adam decides that Rebecca must earn help himself, since giving it openly would cause remark.
Miss Maxwell goes South every spring vacation, traveling by sea to Old Point Comfort.
Miss Maxwell says she would like nothing better than to have Rebecca as a companion on the trip.
Adam says he has been interested in Rebecca for some years and that she was a friend of his long before Miss Maxwell came to Wareham.
Miss Maxwell says she discovered Rebecca herself.
Miss Maxwell says Rebecca attends to her own development and is in a sense independent of everything and everybody.
